pr_body:
# Overview

Fixes https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/17869.

# Summary

`WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO` changes various limits on `RenderDevice`. This is useful to simulate platforms with lower limits.

However, some plugins only check the limits on `RenderAdapter` (the actual GPU) - these limits are not affected by `WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO`. So the plugins try to use features that are unavailable and wgpu says "oh no". See https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/17869 for details.

The PR adds various checks on `RenderDevice` limits. This is enough to get most examples working, but some are not fixed (see below).

# Testing

- Tested native, with and without "WGPU_SETTINGS=webgl2". Win10/Vulkan/Nvidia".
- Also WebGL. Win10/Chrome/Nvidia.

```
$env:WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO = "webgl2"
cargo run --example testbed_3d
cargo run --example testbed_2d
cargo run --example testbed_ui
cargo run --example deferred_rendering
cargo run --example many_lights
cargo run --example order_independent_transparency # Still broken, see below.
cargo run --example occlusion_culling # Still broken, see below.
```

# Not Fixed

While testing I found a few other cases of limits being broken. 

"Compatibility" settings (WebGPU minimums) breaks native in various examples.

```
$env:WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO = "compatibility"
cargo run --example testbed_3d

  In Device::create_bind_group_layout, label = 'build mesh uniforms GPU early occlusion culling bind group layout'
    Too many bindings of type StorageBuffers in Stage ShaderStages(COMPUTE), limit is 8, count was 9. Check the limit `max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage` passed to `Adapter::request_device`
```

`occlusion_culling` breaks fake webgl.
```
$env:WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO = "webgl2"
cargo run --example occlusion_culling

thread '<unnamed>' panicked at C:\Projects\bevy\crates\bevy_render\src\render_resource\pipeline_cache.rs:555:28:
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 2
Encountered a panic in system `bevy_render::renderer::render_system`!
```

`occlusion_culling` breaks real webgl.

```
cargo run --example occlusion_culling --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

ERROR app: panicked at C:\Users\T\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f\glow-0.16.0\src\web_sys.rs:4223:9:
Tex storage 2D multisample is not supported
```

OIT breaks fake webgl.

```
$env:WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO = "webgl2"
cargo run --example order_independent_transparency

  In Device::create_bind_group, label = 'mesh_view_bind_group'
    Number of bindings in bind group descriptor (28) does not match the number of bindings defined in the bind group layout (25)

```

OIT breaks real webgl

```
cargo run --example order_independent_transparency --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

  In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'pbr_oit_mesh_pipeline'
    Error matching ShaderStages(FRAGMENT) shader requirements against the pipeline
      Shader global ResourceBinding { group: 0, binding: 34 } is not available in the pipeline layout
        Binding is missing from the pipeline layout
```
pr_comments: If we can get this setup in CI, I would love automated tests for this. It's not feasible to manually test this kind of stuff myself, but it would be really nice to have CI let me know when we're going above WebGL2 or WebGPU minspec.
Updated to address a few concerns - no functional changes, just refactoring and tweaking warnings.

issue_context.title: `WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO=webgl2` causes panics
issue_context.body:
## TLDR

Some rendering plugins may panic after trying to use wgpu features that have been disabled by the `WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO` env var. The solution might be to add more checks.

## Bevy version

0.16-dev 15b795d7d6a97fd4006dd2c1233050662327dcce

## System info

```
SystemInfo { os: "Windows 10 Pro", kernel: "19045" }
AdapterInfo { name: "NVIDIA GeForce GT 1030", vendor: 4318, device: 7425, device_type: DiscreteGpu, driver: "NVIDIA", driver_info: "560.94", backend: Vulkan }
```

## What you did

I wanted to test what happens if the renderer's skinning pipeline uses uniform buffers. I was too lazy to make a real wasm build, so after a discord suggestion I tried the `WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO` env var. This is a Bevy feature - see `settings_priority_from_env()`.

```sh
WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO=webgl2
# Or for windows powershell: $env:WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO = "webgl2"

cargo run --example animated_mesh
```

(Side note: shouldn't a Bevy env var start with `BEVY_`?)

## What went wrong

```
thread 'main' panicked at wgpu-24.0.1\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:1079:26:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Device::create_bind_group_layout, label = 'oit_resolve_bind_group_layout'
    Too many bindings of type StorageBuffers in Stage ShaderStages(FRAGMENT), limit is 0, count was 2. Check the limit `max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage` passed to `Adapter::request_device`

stack backtrace:
    ...
   8: bevy_render::renderer::render_device::RenderDevice::create_bind_group_layout<ref$<str$> >
             at .\crates\bevy_render\src\renderer\render_device.rs:146
   9: bevy_core_pipeline::oit::resolve::impl$1::from_world
             at .\crates\bevy_core_pipeline\src\oit\resolve\mod.rs:93    
```

## So what's going on?

`WGPU_SETTINGS_PRIO=webgl2` causes `WgpuSettings::limits` to be initialized to `wgpu::Limits::downlevel_webgl2_defaults()`, which `initialize_renderer()` then passes into `wgpu::DeviceDescriptor`.

This overrides the limits reported by `RenderDevice`. However, some rendering plugins check for limits on the `RenderAdapter`, not the `RenderDevice`. `RenderAdapter` does not respect the overridden limits - it's reports what the hardware can really do.

Example from `OitResolvePlugin::finish()`:

```rust
if !render_app
    .world()
    .resource::<RenderAdapter>()
    .get_downlevel_capabilities()
    .flags
    .contains(DownlevelFlags::FRAGMENT_WRITABLE_STORAGE)
{
    warn!("OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin not loaded. GPU lacks support: DownlevelFlags::FRAGMENT_WRITABLE_STORAGE.");
    return;
}
```

## Can you fix it?

I can't see any way to set the adapter's limits. So I think the solution might be to check the device limits, either instead of or in addition to checking the adapter. But it's clunky, and the limits are expressed in different ways.

```rust
if render_app
    .world()
    .resource::<RenderDevice>()
    .limits()
    .max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage
    < 2
{
    warn!("OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin not loaded. GPU lacks support: max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage < 2.");
    return;
}
```

There are four cases that I can see - search for `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS` and `DownlevelFlags::FRAGMENT_WRITABLE_STORAGE`.

I can have a crack at a PR if a render expert can confirm that the suggested fix is the right direction.

review_comments:
The `warn: bool` is a bit smelly, but wasn't sure if an enum was justified for two calls.

Also considered putting the warning behind a `OnceLock`, but that's technically kinda wrong as the warning is specifically about the plugin not loading.
It might be nice to return after all compatibility checks are printed, but this is good enough as is
